I don't see any use case of this code in this commit. It is not setting up any context and it is not a stub commit.
So IMO this should not be part of this commit.
Done
can we say i_afruJsonObj or i_fruJsonObj
Done
is it better to send whole object {"Eeprom": []}, so it will be simple to construct chassis based JSON for m_chassisIdToJsonMap
Addressed.
should API name be updateMapForFru or updateMapForAFru , as its updating map data for a single FRU ?

"Updating" means there is some data present already, and we are updating that data. This API is building the maps, and creating entries in the EEPROM to chassis ID map and chassis ID to chassis JSON object map.
Acknowledged
isn't first-second steps doing this already, do we need iteration ?
Done
should we log a info PEL here ?

How will a PEL help here? In failure case, a FRU's entry won't be there in the maps. `getJsonObj()` should handle the scenario where for a given FRU, chassis specific JSON entry is not found in the map.

getJsonObj() return main JSON if entry not in EEPROM to JSON map.
but while building config JSON map had any exception that will exclude adding entry to the map, hence need to use main JSON which will take more time in case of search.

So here while building chassis specific JSON, we could have logged a PEL which helps in debugging later.

anyway we can check logging PEL required later, if such instances occur frequently.
is commonInterfaces a mandatory tag, do we need to log if not ?

As of today, `commonInterfaces` is not mandatory for building the chassis specific maps, but we should still log it if it is not found in the main system config JSON, as it indicates the system config JSON may have missing data.
as you mentioned commonInterfaces in not mandatory, we should had log when it become mandatory field. which ever system doesn't have commonInterface will have unnecessary log for that system now.
I said `commonInterfaces` is not mandatory for building the chassis specific maps. We still have `commonInterfaces` tag in all P11, PST system JSONs.
As discussed, removing this log.

instead, can we declare l_commonJsonObj as std::optional<nlohmann::json> with std::nullopt and update the variable if there is commonInterfaces. And we can avoid this ternary operator here in the for loop.
Done
I see implementation as well, why are we mixing stubs and implementation together?
This commit implements `buildChassisToFruMap` API and introduces stub implementation of helper method `buildMapsForFru` which is used by `buildChassisToFruMap`.

>. This commit implements buildChassisToFruMap API

But I don't see anything related to this in header, the header only says about stub implementation.
Addressed.
Acknowledged
Blank line missing.
Done
Who is calling this API? I need to get the use case..
Getting called from constructor, ignore the comment.
This API is being called in the constructor, which has been merged.
Why a private API checking validity of a member variable?
Since it is called directly from constructor, as as exception we can have it checked here. Ignore the comment.
Member variable can be modified by any other API. Since this API is using system config JSON, it should validate it before using.

>  Member variable can be modified by any other API

Yes, but private members are not exposed and are not called by external world and that is why the responsibility of these kind of validation lies with the called public method which gave the execution passage to the private API.
Call to private methods are through a controlled passage and hence from a good design perspective that passage should filter the call if it is invalid.

Whereas, public methods are exposed to the external world and can be called by anyone, the coder does not have control on that, hence these checks are required there.

Having said that, since this is a direct call from constructor, its ok to have it here.
Done

Are we adding common interface JSON to all the logical JSONs?
If so what is the use case of doing so?
We had decided to add it as per our design discussion, in order to keep the chassis specific JSON structure as close as possible to the actual system configuration JSON.
Ok, but thinking about it now, I am not able to see a use case, do you have any in mind? If not we can always comeback and add this when required, why to carry the baggage from now?
We will keep it for now to keep it consistent with the base JSON format.
